passages.note: House Third Reading roll call on SB1165, a single-subject biological-sex athletics bill, records Martinez voting Y in a divided 31-24 passage.

passages.provision_quote: A. Each interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport that is sponsored by a public school or a private school whose students or teams compete against a public school shall be expressly designated as one of the following based on the biological sex of the students who participate on the team or in the sport: 1. "Males", "men" or "boys". 2. "Females", "women" or "girls". 3. "Coed" or "mixed". B. Athletic teams or sports designated for "females", "women" or "girls" may not be open to students of the male sex. C. This section does not restrict the eligibility of any student to participate in any interscholastic or intramural athletic team or sport designated as being for "males", "men" or "boys" or designated as "coed" or "mixed".
passages.note: The enacted statute restricts only female-designated teams to the biological female sex and expressly leaves male and coed teams unrestricted, excluding rung 5.

rows.reasoning: Martinez voted Y on the House Third Reading final passage of SB 1165 (2022), the Save Women's Sports Act, whose operative text designates teams by biological sex and bars students of the male sex from female-designated teams while leaving male and coed teams unrestricted, matching "require transgender athletes to compete only on teams matching their biological sex assigned at birth" and excluding a complete ban on all organized sport.
